verses.text: As they got close to Jerusalem and reached Bethphage on the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent two disciples ahead.
He told them, “Go to the village across from you. Right away, you’ll find a donkey tied up, with her colt beside her. Untie them and bring them to me.”
“If anyone asks what you’re doing, say, ‘The Lord needs them.’ They’ll send them right over.”
This happened to fulfill what the prophet had spoken:
“‘Tell Zion’s daughter: Look, your King is coming to you, humble and riding on a donkey—on a colt, a young donkey.’”
The disciples went and did exactly what Jesus told them.
They brought the donkey and colt, laid their clothes on them, and Jesus sat down.
A huge crowd spread their clothes across the road. Others cut branches from the trees and laid them down too.
The crowds in front of Jesus and behind him kept shouting, “Hosanna to David’s Son! Blessed is the one who comes in the Lord’s name! Hosanna in the highest!”
When Jesus entered Jerusalem, the whole city was buzzing: “Who is this?”
The crowds answered, “This is the prophet Jesus, from Nazareth in Galilee.”
Jesus went into God’s temple and drove out everyone buying and selling there. He flipped the money-changers’ tables and the seats of those selling doves.
He told them, “Scripture says, ‘My house will be called a house of prayer,’ but you’ve turned it into a hideout for robbers!”
Blind people and people who couldn’t walk came to him in the temple, and he healed them.
The chief priests and teachers of the Law saw the amazing things he did, and heard children shouting in the temple, “Hosanna to David’s Son!” They were furious.
They asked him, “Do you hear what these kids are saying?” Jesus said, “Yes. Have you never read, ‘You’ve made praise perfect from the mouths of children and babies’?”
He left them, went out of the city to Bethany, and stayed there for the night.
Early the next morning, as Jesus headed back to the city, he was hungry.
He saw a fig tree beside the road and went over, but it had nothing on it except leaves. He said, “You’ll never bear fruit again!” The tree dried up right away.
The disciples were amazed. “How did the fig tree dry up so fast?” they asked.

Jesus answered, “I’m telling you the truth: if you have faith and don’t doubt, you’ll do what happened to this fig tree—and even tell this mountain, ‘Get lifted up and thrown into the sea,’ and it’ll happen.”
“Whatever you ask for in prayer with faith, you’ll receive.”
Jesus went into the temple to teach. The chief priests and elders came up and asked, “What authority do you have to do these things? Who gave it to you?”
Jesus answered, “I’ll ask you one question. If you answer me, I’ll tell you what authority I have to do these things.”
“John’s baptism—where did it come from, heaven or people?” They talked it over: “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ he’ll ask, ‘Then why didn’t you believe John?’”
“But if we say, ‘From people,’ we’re scared of the crowd. Everyone considers John a prophet.”
So they answered Jesus, “We don’t know.” He told them, “Then I won’t tell you what authority I have to do these things.”
“What do you think? A man had two sons. He went to the first and said, ‘Son, go work in the vineyard today.’”
“The son answered, ‘I’m not going.’ But later he changed his mind and went.”
“The father went to the second son and said the same. He answered, ‘I’m going, sir,’ but didn’t go.”
“Which son did what his father wanted?” They answered, “The first.” Jesus told them, “I’m telling you the truth: tax collectors and prostitutes are entering God’s Kingdom ahead of you.”
“John came showing you the way of righteousness, but you didn’t believe him. The tax collectors and prostitutes did. Even after you saw that, you didn’t change your minds and believe him.”
“Listen to another story. A landowner planted a vineyard, fenced it in, dug a winepress, built a tower, rented it to farmers, and went to another country.”
“When harvest time came close, he sent servants to the farmers to collect his share of the fruit.”
“The farmers grabbed his servants, beat one, killed another, and stoned another.”
“He sent more servants than before, but the farmers treated them the same way.”
“Finally, he sent his son, thinking, ‘They’ll respect my son.’”
“But when the farmers saw the son, they said, ‘This is the heir. Come on, let’s kill him and take what he’s going to inherit.’”
“They grabbed him, threw him outside the vineyard, and killed him.”
“So when the vineyard owner comes, what do you think he’ll do to those farmers?”
They answered, “He’ll destroy those wicked men and rent the vineyard to other farmers who’ll give him the fruit when it’s due.”
Jesus said, “Haven’t you read in Scripture, ‘The stone the builders rejected became the cornerstone. The Lord did this, and it’s amazing to see’?”
“So I’m telling you, God’s Kingdom will be taken from you and given to a people who produce its fruit.”
“Anyone who falls on this stone will be broken apart. If it falls on someone, it’ll crush them.”
When the chief priests and Pharisees heard his stories, they realized he was talking about them.
They wanted to arrest him, but they feared the crowds, because the people considered Jesus a prophet.
